title: Microsoft Copilot Dashboard: export de-identified user-level Copilot metrics
summary: The briefing's default, licensing prerequisites, export behaviour and policy commands are supported. The revised PowerShell guidance does not contradict it. The policy routes should incorporate the feature selections currently supplied in their notes, and the access-inventory and audit checklist steps lack corresponding control rows.

claims.quote: This enables users to export row-level Copilot metrics from the Copilot Dashboard for reporting and deeper analysis.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].governs; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Viva feature access policies can disable Copilot export at tenant or group level, with feature policies generally supporting user scopes too.
claims.quote: Global admins can disable or re-enable the feature for the tenant or specific groups through Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM) in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The export policy route is Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Access setting, with the note directing selection of Viva Insights and Copilot Metrics Export.
claims.quote: Select Create a policy. ... Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off
claims.fix: Include the app and feature selection already given in the note in the route: 'Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Viva Insights > Copilot Metrics Export > Access setting'. Retain the note that Learn calls the setting User-level export and insights. See https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/control-access-admin-center.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId <FeatureId from Get-VivaModuleFeature> -Name <policy name> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone creates a tenant-wide disabling policy for the selected feature.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone

claims.claim: The web app policy route is Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Access setting, with the note directing selection of the Viva Insights web app feature.
claims.quote: Select Create a policy. ... Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off
claims.fix: Include the app and feature selection already given in the note in the route: 'Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Viva Insights > Viva Insights web app > Access setting'. See https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/control-access-admin-center.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId "Viva Insights web app" -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone disables the web app tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Example: Turn off the Viva Insights web app for all users in your tenant ... ModuleId : VivaInsights ... FeatureId : Viva Insights web app ... Name : DisableFeatureForAll ... IsFeatureEnabled : false ... Everyone
